analytic_dependency.name: QFORM-RANK2-AFFINE-HALF-RIESZ-v1
analytic_dependency.scope: For U with two orthonormal columns, invertible symmetric 2x2 Lambda and arbitrary affine b, sup_s E|quadratic+affine-s|^{-1/2} <=128|det Lambda|^{-1/4}.

new_result.name: QFORM-GROUPED-SCHUR-RANK2-OUTSIDE-FREE-v1
new_result.statement: If a=A_ii is nonzero and the principal block S_JJ of the scalar-pivot Schur complement on an original-coordinate bank J has exact rank two with nonzero eigenvalues mu1,mu2 and Delta2=|mu1 mu2|, then ||p_{X^TAX}||_infinity <=128 |a|^{-1/2} Delta2^{-1/4}, uniformly over all remaining Schur quadratic terms, all cross couplings, and arbitrary independent cap-one input laws.
new_result.translation_localization_feature: Complete square only in the original pivot coordinate; condition on all outside coordinates. Outside cross terms become arbitrary affine terms in the active bank. The scalar shell estimate is uniform in the resulting correlated translation, and partner mass-linear localization gives zero outside-fragment tax.

target_family_closed: A=[[1,0,0],[0,J_m/m direct_sum -J_m/m,C],[0,C^T,D]] has at least eigenvalues >=1,>=1,<=-1 by interlacing for arbitrary C,D and obeys density <=128 for all independent cap-one laws.
correction_compatibility: QFORM-O1-PIVOT-SCALE-FROM-MASS-FALSE-v1 does not contradict this theorem: no scalar pivot lower bound is inferred. The theorem explicitly pays |a|^{-1/2}; the near-zero/zero pivot branch remains unpaid.
unresolved_implication: Give an exhaustive quantitative original-coordinate reduction from the bare three-large-eigenvalue hypothesis to a diffuse/ridge branch, a nondegenerate grouped rank-two Schur bank with bounded |a|^{-1/2}Delta2^{-1/4}, or another mass-linear grouped mechanism; separately handle the zero/near-zero scalar-pivot transition rather than deriving pivot scale from determinant mass.
next_step: Fuse this grouped nonzero-pivot branch with the corrected zero/near-zero hyperbolic O1 packet and ridge-heavy branch, without fixed-small-minor extraction or normalization of thin slices.
